1	# Drawer + Tabs (SFCC-195, SFCC-736) — plan
2	
3	_Built incrementally with Tim, walking real Figma frames and Jira tickets, in `feature/sfcc-52-global-header`'s session on 2026-08-26/27. Saved here per the SFCC-52 precedent (`.docs/temp/SFCC-52-global-header-plan.md`) for review before any component code is written._
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	Building a reusable slide-out Drawer (right-anchored) and a reusable Tabs component for
8	Zimmermann PWA. Immediate scope is two stories:
9	
10	- **SFCC-736 "pdp/drawer"** (assigned to Tim, Squad-A, In Progress) — the drawer _shell_ only:
11	  slide-in panel, backdrop overlay, close button, tab navigation header. Accepts tab content as
12	  children. Does not own tab content.
13	- **SFCC-195 "PDP – Slide Out - Details & Care"** — first tab's content (Details & Care),
14	  triggered by info links on PDP. Depends on SFCC-736's shell/tab API.
15	
16	Known future consumers of the same Drawer/Tabs primitives (NOT in scope now, but the API must
17	stay generic enough for them): SFCC-102 (Size & Fit tab), SFCC-266 (EU Environmental Qualities
18	tab), SFCC-267 (Shipping & Returns + Assistance tabs), SFCC-101 (Measmerize/Find My Size CTA),
19	SFCC-742 (Wishlist login panel — renders as children inside pdp/drawer), SFCC-801 (global
20	country/currency selector — separate right-anchored drawer, same shape), **SFCC-297 (Find in
21	Boutique — confirmed by Tim to use this same Drawer)**. A story also exists for the Add to Cart /
22	View Cart mini-cart (not yet shared/ticketed here) — confirmed by Tim it will invoke this Drawer
23	to display the mini-cart once picked up, consistent with `cart.md` PRD's "opens as an overlay on
24	Add to Bag CTA or bag icon click."
25	
26	## Research findings
27	
28	- **No existing Tabs component anywhere** — not in `overrides/`, not in the base
29	  `@salesforce/retail-react-app` template (confirmed via full grep, zero `Tabs`/`TabList` usage
30	  and no theme recipe). Genuinely greenfield, no in-repo prior art.
31	- **`ZimmModal` + `useZimmModal`** (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmModal/`,
32	  `overrides/app/hooks/useZimmModal.ts`) exist today but are fully hand-rolled — NOT built on
33	  Chakra's `Modal`/`Drawer` primitives. Centered/fixed-width only, no `placement` concept. Single
34	  consumer: `ZimmSubscribeModal` (newsletter capture, footer). Not Tier 2 yet (only 1 consumer).
35	  **Decision (updated): refactor in place onto Chakra's `Modal` primitive** — see Decisions made.
36	- **Add to Cart is NOT greenfield at the data layer.** `useShopperBasketsMutationHelper().
37	addItemToNewOrExistingBasket(productItems)` (from `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`) + existing
38	  `useCurrentBasket()` (inherited unmodified, Tier 1) already handle the full add-to-basket flow.
39	  A fully-wired confirmation UI already exists too: `AddToCartModal` +
40	  `AddToCartModalProvider`/`useAddToCartModalContext()` (base
41	  `app/hooks/use-add-to-cart-modal.js`), mounted at app root, built on Chakra `Modal` (not
42	  Drawer). No mini-cart/cart-drawer exists in the base app yet. **Tim confirmed a story already
43	  exists** for this (not yet shared) — when picked up, it will invoke our new Drawer to display
44	  the mini-cart. The correct approach is shadowing `use-add-to-cart-modal.js` and swapping its
45	  Modal primitives for our Drawer, reusing the existing context/hook plumbing and data layer
46	  as-is — not building new cart data logic.
47	- **`protectedFiles.md`'s Tier 2 "Shared Hooks" list is NOT aspirational** (correcting an earlier
48	  wrong read) — all 8 named hooks (`use-auth-modal`, `use-toast`, `use-modal-state`,
49	  `use-intersection-observer`, `use-currency`, `use-dnt-notification`, `use-app-origin`,
50	  `use-selected-store`) exist fully-built in the base template today, several genuinely
51	  5+-consumer, none stubs. They just aren't overridden in `overrides/` yet. Tier 2 protection
52	  applies the moment one is overridden.
53	  - **`use-modal-state.js`** (base): `useModalState({closeOnRouteChange, resetDataOnClose}) =>
54	{isOpen, data, onOpen(data), onClose()}`, auto-closes on route change. Currently 3 consumers
55	    in base (bonus-product-selection-modal subsystem).
56	  - **`use-auth-modal.js`** (base): `AuthModal` component + `useAuthModal(initialView)` — full
57	    login/register/reset/passwordless modal system, already reused 3x (`_app`,
58	    `with-registration` gate wrapper, checkout contact-info). Directly relevant to SFCC-742
59	    (wishlist login panel) — the `with-registration` wrapper is a reusable gate-the-action
60	    pattern, not something to build fresh.
61	- **Base `drawer-menu`** (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/drawer-menu/
62	drawer-menu.jsx`, inherited unmodified in this repo) is a real, working Chakra `Drawer`
63	  implementation: `Drawer`/`DrawerOverlay`/`DrawerContent`/`DrawerHeader`/`DrawerBody`/
64	  `DrawerFooter`/`DrawerCloseButton`, `placement="left"`, responsive `size` via
65	  `useBreakpointValue`, multi-part theme styling via `useMultiStyleConfig('DrawerMenu')`
66	  (project theme file `theme/components/project/drawer-menu.js`), focus-trap/scroll-lock
67	  inherited for free from Chakra (not hand-rolled). This is the reference pattern for the new
68	  drawer.
69	- **PRD vocabulary is deliberate**: `pdp.md` distinguishes "slide-out/flyout" from "modal" in 3
70	  places (Find in Boutique, Size Guide). `checkout.md` contradicted this once (calls Find in
71	  Boutique a "modal") — **fixed**: `checkout.md`'s CFD-043 line now says "Find in Boutique
72	  drawer," consistent with `pdp.md` and with Find in Boutique (SFCC-297) confirmed as a Drawer
73	  consumer. `homepage.md`'s "Join Us" capture (already built as `ZimmSubscribeModal`) is a
74	  genuine confirmed centered Modal — so both patterns are real and intentionally distinct in
75	  this codebase.
76	
77	## Decisions made
78	
79	1. **New Drawer built on Chakra's native `Drawer` primitive**, following the `drawer-menu`
80	   precedent — inherits focus-trap/scroll-lock/ESC handling from Chakra for free. Styled
81	   entirely via a new Zimmermann project theme recipe (co-located `.css.ts` per
82	   `overrideStyling.md`'s pattern), not inline props.
83	2. **The "generic hook for other developers" is an override of base's `use-modal-state.js`**
84	   (`overrides/app/hooks/use-modal-state.ts`), not a new custom hook — this becomes Tier 2
85	   protected the moment it's created, per `protectedFiles.md`.
86	3. **One Modal system, not two — `ZimmModal`/`useZimmModal` refactored in place onto Chakra's
87	   `Modal` primitive** (updated from an earlier "leave it untouched, two architectures coexist"
88	   draft — Tim doesn't want two different dialog implementations in the codebase). Same
89	   component name, same public props (`isOpen`, `mounted`, `onClose`, `maxWidth`, `labelledBy`,
90	   `describedBy`, `children`) and same hook name/shape as far as the one existing consumer
91	   (`ZimmSubscribeModal`) needs — only the internals swap from the hand-rolled

617	Tim reported: pressing Tab inside an open drawer moves between the active tab and the close
618	icon instead of cycling the other tab headers, and asked for Tab-to-move/Enter-to-activate
619	behaviour. Checked this against the actual spec before changing anything (WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.1 +
620	WAI-ARIA APG's Tabs pattern, both fetched live) rather than assuming either the bug report or a
621	"just make it accessible" reflex fix was right:
622	
623	- **WCAG 2.1.1 doesn't mandate Tab-based navigation for a composite widget** — any keyboard
624	  path satisfies it.
625	- **WAI-ARIA's Tabs pattern is explicit**: `Tab` moves focus into/out of the tablist as a whole
626	  (arrives on the active tab, leaves to the next focusable element outside it — the close icon,
627	  here); Left/Right/Home/End move *within* the tablist. Two activation models exist —
628	  **automatic** (arrow keys switch the panel immediately, no Enter needed) is recommended
629	  specifically "when panel content is not costly to display," which is exactly this case
630	  (static content, no fetch). **Manual** (Enter/Space required) is for the opposite case.
631	- `ZimmTabs` already implemented automatic activation with Left/Right and a roving tabIndex —
632	  the reported "bug" was actually the Tab key behaving per spec. Confirmed with Tim to keep
633	  automatic activation and fix the real, separate gap instead: no `aria-controls`/`id` linking
634	  each tab to its panel, so a screen reader couldn't announce what a tab controls.

638	  prop (the tablist itself needs an accessible name — no visible on-page label exists for it,
639	  per APG) and `idPrefix` prop, each tab now gets `id={idPrefix}-tab-{tab.id}` and
640	  `aria-controls={idPrefix}-panel`.

642	  `ZimmDrawer` also mounted on the same page); its panel now has `id={idPrefix}-panel`,

644	  `tabIndex={0}` — the last one is its own separate APG recommendation (a tabpanel needs to be
645	  in the Tab sequence when its content isn't itself reliably focusable), so `Tab` from the
646	  active tab now lands in the panel content before reaching the close icon.

33	ROW also routed via `/en-ch/` and `/en-ca/` prefixes (DMU-013; see [dataMigrationSeo.md](dataMigrationSeo.md) for full URL strategy). AU configured as root with no locale prefix and designated x-default hreflang target (DMU-016, **Resolved** — the AU root remains globally crawlable because search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt from the human geo-redirect; see REG-009 in Section 4).
34	
35	URL formats: product `/[prefix]/[name]-[colour].html` (the `.html` suffix is **preserved** to maintain existing indexed URLs — DMU-015); category `/[prefix]/[slug]` (no `.html`). Category URLs are updated for SEO consolidation (e.g. `/clothing/dresses`) with 301 redirects from all legacy paths (DMU-014).
36	
37	Business users can manage storefront configuration in SFCC BM at both global and individual storefront levels (REG-010).
38	
39	The US storefront supports all required US address formats; APO, FPO, and PO Box addresses are **not** supported (REG-012).
40	
41	### Country → Storefront routing (Country to Storefront Mapping sheet)
42	
43	The full per-country mapping lives in the source sheet; the FE only needs the routing logic:
44	
45	- **AU (root):** Australia (default) and all Oceania — American Samoa, Cook Islands, Fiji, Guam, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Micronesia, Nauru, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Niue, Northern Marianas, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu. NZ and New Caledonia get Avalara duty/tax; other Oceania destinations are DDU (REG-003).
46	- **UK (`/uk/`):** United Kingdom only.
47	- **US (`/us/` domestic):** United States (default) and **Puerto Rico**.
48	- **US (`/en-ca/` international, Global-e):** Canada, Mexico, and all other Americas — Caribbean, Central America, and South America (Argentina, Aruba, Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Bermuda, Bolivia, Brazil, BVI, Cayman, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominica, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Grenada, Guatemala, Guyana, Haiti, Honduras, Jamaica, Nicaragua, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, St Kitts & Nevis, St Lucia, St Vincent, Trinidad & Tobago, Turks & Caicos, USVI, Uruguay, Venezuela, etc.).
49	- **EU domestic (`/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/`):** France (default), Germany, Italy, Spain, Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, Austria, Ireland, Portugal, Greece, **Denmark**, Sweden, Finland, Poland, Czechia, Hungary, Romania, Bulgaria, Croatia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Cyprus, Malta, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Andorra, Monaco, San Marino.
50	- **EU international (`/en-ch/`, Global-e):** Non-EU Europe (Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Albania, Bosnia & Herzegovina, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Gibraltar, Greenland, Faroe Islands, Channel Islands, etc.) and **all of Africa** (Algeria, Angola, Benin, Botswana, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, Cape Verde, Chad, Comoros, Congo, Côte d'Ivoire, Djibouti, Equatorial Guinea, Ethiopia, Gabon, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritania, Mauritius, Morocco, Mozambique, Namibia, Nigeria, Réunion, São Tomé, Senegal, Seychelles, Sierra Leone, South Africa, Swaziland, Tanzania, Togo, Tunisia, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe). Also includes Falkland Islands, French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Mayotte, Saint Barthélemy, Saint Helena, Saint Martin, Suriname.
51	- **HK (`/hk/`, Global-e):** Hong Kong (default), China, Macau, Taiwan, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines, India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Brunei, Cambodia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Laos, Maldives, Mongolia, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Tajikistan, Timor-Leste, Uzbekistan. **Also includes "Australia" as a destination** — this is the REG-027 path for non-Oceania clients who select AU in the country selector (they are routed to HK, not the gated AU site).
52	- **ME (`/en-ae/`, Global-e):** UAE (default), Bahrain, Egypt, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia.
53	
54	**Denmark routing is resolved → EU Domestic** (Country to Storefront Mapping sheet confirms; remove from Open Items).
55	
56	> Geographic anomalies (mapping sheet): Falkland Islands, French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Mayotte, Saint Barthélemy, Saint Helena, Saint Martin, Suriname all route to **EU International** despite being in the Americas/African geography. This follows fulfilment territory, not landmass — flagged for awareness; routing tables must follow the sheet verbatim.
57	
58	---
59	
60	## 2. Entry Routing & Mismatch Detection (REG-009, REG-013 – REG-035)
61	
62	- **IP geolocation** selects the site on first visit (REG-013).
63	- **AU is gated** to AU and NZ/Pacific Island IPs only (REG-009). AU is the `x-default` hreflang and must remain crawlable, so it is never blocked at the network level. A non-AU/non-Oceania human visitor landing on AU is redirected server-side to their matched storefront before AUD pricing renders; if no storefront matches their region, fall back to HK. Search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt from the redirect — match by User-Agent against a comprehensive allowlist (Googlebot incl. Image/News, Bingbot, DuckDuckBot, AppleBot, YandexBot, Baiduspider, Slackbot, Twitterbot, facebookexternalhit, LinkedInBot, WhatsApp, Discordbot). Fail open: if UA looks botty but isn't matched, skip the redirect rather than apply it — false-positive cost is zero, missing a real crawler hurts SEO.
64	- All other storefronts use **mismatch detection** (REG-014): a country slide-out is shown on the first visit if the user's IP country does not match the storefront's shipping region (REG-015). Two CTAs: redirect to the appropriate storefront, or open the country selector (REG-016). A warning is shown that changing location may remove items from the bag (REG-017). Not shown if country matches (REG-018). Shown on first visit only — does not reappear after selection or dismissal (REG-019).
65	- **Country + language selector** available on all storefronts except AU (REG-020, REG-025). Countries grouped by region (Asia/Oceania, Europe, Americas) with currency display and search field (REG-021). Warning shown that changing location may remove items from the bag (REG-022). Country and language combined in the same selector; EU domestic offers EN/FR/IT/ES, all other storefronts English only (REG-023). Selected EU locale reflected in URL (REG-024).
66	- AU is gated and does **not** allow inbound cross-navigation from other sites (REG-025).
67	- **China** selected from any country selector routes to HK (REG-026).
68	- **Australia** selected from another storefront's country selector (i.e. clients outside Oceania) routes to HK (REG-027).
69	- Global-e checkout locks the shipping country — determined by country selector pre-checkout, cannot be changed inside Global-e (REG-028).
70	
71	### EU language mismatch (REG-029 – REG-035)
72	
73	When a user's GEO-IP country doesn't match the URL language on the EU domestic storefront, show a language mismatch modal in the current URL language (REG-029, REG-031). Two CTAs: continue in current language, or switch (REG-032). Country-to-language mapping (REG-030):
74	
75	- France / Monaco → French (`/fr-eu/`)
76	- Italy / San Marino → Italian (`/it-eu/`)
77	- Spain → Spanish (`/es-eu/`)
78	
79	Modal does not show when detected country matches the current URL language (REG-033), and is not shown for countries with no dedicated EU locale — they default to `/en-eu/` (REG-034). Logic applies regardless of entry point (Instagram, Google Shopping, direct URL, organic search) (REG-035).
80	
81	---
82	
83	## 3. Checkout Ownership
84	
85	- **SFCC** owns domestic checkout for AU (REG-003), UK (REG-004), US domestic (REG-005), EU domestic (REG-006 dom).
86	- **Global-e** owns checkout for HK (REG-007), ME (REG-008), US international (REG-005 — now a separate SFCC site), EU international (REG-006 intl) — and for any domestic storefront when the customer's selected shipping destination is outside the domestic market.
87	- **AU serves Oceania (NZ, New Caledonia, Pacific Islands) domestically** via SFCC — not via Global-e. Avalara calculates duties/tax for NZ and New Caledonia specifically (REG-003); other Oceania destinations are DDU.
88	- Branch checkout ownership at PDP/cart, not only at the checkout page.
89	- **Global-e pricing via SFCC price books (REG-041, Confirmed 05-05):** SFCC holds all price books including for Global-e markets. AP21 feeds base RRP pricebooks per currency (AUD, EUR, GBP, USD) and fixed pricelists per Global-e market to SFCC via MuleSoft. A nightly job generates Global-e-derived pricebooks using FX rates and coefficients from Global-e. Global-e handles shipping charges, duties, and taxes at checkout. SFCC sends the complete cart in the target currency to Global-e. SFCC does **not** independently calculate shipping, duties, or tax for Global-e paths. (REG-040 was retired 05-05 — superseded by REG-041.)
90	
91	_For checkout-specific frontend behaviour (redirect trigger, data flow), see [checkout.md](checkout.md)._
92	
93	---
94	
95	## 4. Currency & Tax (REG-036 – REG-042)
96	
97	- Single currency per domestic storefront: AUD, USD, GBP, EUR (REG-039). No multi-currency toggle. (Open: Zimmermann would like multi-currency on AU domestic to offer NZD — not yet agreed.)
98	- Tax display: AU (GST), UK (VAT) via SFCC native tax tables, EU domestic (VAT) via Avalara (REG-037). The EU domestic site supports one RRP but must support multiple EU zone VAT requirements in the order payload. US domestic: prices excl. tax; Avalara calculates sales tax at checkout (REG-038). NZ and New Caledonia on AU: Avalara (REG-037).
99	- Sale pricing: was/now format. If price changes again after sale, only "now" updates; "was" is retained (REG-042).
100	- Prices shown in storefront currency on PDP, PLP, mini-cart, cart (REG-036).
101	
102	---
103	
104	## 5. EU Locale Billing Fields (REG-011)
105	
106	The system will display locale-specific additional billing fields where required (e.g. Italian Codice Fiscale or VAT ID). **Open (REG-011):** confirm with Egaltine which other locales (e.g. Spanish NIF, French SIRET) require additional fields. Do not implement until confirmed.
107	
108	---
109	
110	## 6. Language & Translation (REG-044 – REG-047)
111	
112	- EU domestic supports 4 languages: EN, FR, IT, ES (REG-044). All other storefronts English only.
113	- All customer-facing content (CMS from Contentful, product data from Product API) translated across EU locale variants (REG-045). CMS must accommodate translation-driven adjustments (e.g. button resize for translated CTAs).
114	- English is the site-wide fallback where translated content is unavailable (REG-046).
115	- Translation pipeline (REG-047, de-scoped 2026-05-25): the end-to-end configurable pipeline requirement was withdrawn. Translation occurs directly between **Contentful and Transperfect** outside the PWA Kit's concern; any SFCC-held strings (e.g. system messages, validation copy) are translated via static JSON files. No FE work required beyond consuming the translated Contentful payloads.
116	
117	---
118	
119	## 7. Consent (Didomi) (REG-048 – REG-056)
120	
121	- Cookie consent banner shown on first visit on all storefronts, managed by Didomi CMP (REG-048). Consent preferences persist across sessions (REG-050).
122	- **Do not load any third-party tracking or marketing script until Didomi consent is granted** (REG-049).
123	- Consent categories: Performance, Analytics, Marketing — Required is non-configurable (REG-051). Subject to legal confirmation but expected to follow existing Didomi process.
124	- Customers can review and update preferences at any time via the storefront (REG-052). Granular consent allowed — individual categories can be toggled independently (REG-053).
125	
126	### Per-storefront defaults (REG-054)
127	
128	| Storefront                   | Default                                          |
129	| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
130	| EU storefronts               | Opted-out (no action = opted-out)                |
131	| US domestic                  | Explicit choice required (no action = opted-out) |
132	| AU, US international, HK, ME | Opted-in by default                              |
133	
134	- GTM integrated with Didomi for **Google Consent Mode v2** signal passing across all storefronts (REG-055).
135	- Hashed email passed to GTM at order confirmation for Enhanced Conversions (REG-056).
136	- Didomi consent notice greys out all site content and prevents interaction until the consent flow completes (HPC-013/014).
137	
138	---
139	
140	## 8. Marketing Opt-In (REG-057 – REG-059)
141	
142	- Marketing opt-in checkbox displayed at two points: guest checkout entry page and account registration page. Unchecked by default on all storefronts **except US (pre-checked)** (REG-057).
143	- Opt-in state sync: FE → SFCC → Omneo → Emarsys. Passed to Omneo on order placement for guests, on account registration for registered customers (REG-058).
144	- Registered customers can update marketing preferences in My Account → synced to Omneo (REG-059).
145	
146	_Open: guest checkout journey & marketing opt-in touchpoints (REG-057, REG-058) — see AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies"._
147	
148	---
149	
150	## 9. Inside Chat (HPC-039 – HPC-040)
151	
152	- Customer support chat widget shown on relevant pages per Inside Chat's own display rules.
153	- Must only be initialised **after Didomi consent** for the relevant category.
154	
155	---
156	
157	## 10. GDPR & Privacy (REG-060 – REG-067)
158	
159	- Right-to-erasure: deletion of customer PII from SFCC including registered accounts, saved addresses, and guest order data (REG-060).
160	- DSAR and erasure requests managed via the SFCC GDPR cartridge, replacing the current manual legal/IT ticketing process (REG-061).
161	- Configurable data retention per market in SFCC BM; auto-purge on expiry (REG-062).
162	- Adyen payment tokens held in SFCC are deleted as part of right-to-erasure (REG-063).
163	- Localised privacy policy per storefront (REG-064).
164	- DSAR export of all PII held in SFCC in a portable, readable format (REG-065).
165	- Consent audit log capturing when and how consent was captured (REG-066).
166	- Breach notification reporting filterable by country and US state (REG-067).
167	
168	---
169	
170	## 11. Data Migration, SEO, GEO & URL
171	
172	This content now lives in its own PRD: [dataMigrationSeo.md](dataMigrationSeo.md), covering Magento→SFCC data migration (DMU-001 – DMU-012), URL strategy and redirects (DMU-013 – DMU-020), SEO (DMU-021 – DMU-041), and GEO routing foundations (DMU-042). Storefront routing, consent, and currency remain in this file.
173	
174	---
175	
176	## 12. Open Items
177	
178	See **AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies"** for the full list. Regional open items (data migration / URL / SEO / GEO open items live in [dataMigrationSeo.md](dataMigrationSeo.md)):
179	
180	- EU locale-specific billing fields (Italian Codice Fiscale, Spanish NIF, French SIRET) — confirmation with Egaltine pending (REG-011)
181	- Global-e + Didomi consent interaction — TBD
182	- Guest checkout journey & marketing opt-in touchpoints (REG-057, REG-058)
183	- Multi-currency on AU domestic to offer NZD — added to enhancement log, **not in go-live scope** (REG-039)
184	
185	**Resolved since previous version:**
186	
187	- US single-vs-separate site (REG-005) — **Updated 2026-07-10** to two separate SFCC sites (US domestic `/us/` via SFCC; US international `/en-ca/` via Global-e). The 2026-06-11 single-site decision has been superseded. New site ID `ZimmermannUSIntl` pending BM confirmation.
188	- Denmark routing — confirmed → EU Domestic via Country to Storefront Mapping sheet
189	- REG-047 translation pipeline — de-scoped (Contentful↔Transperfect direct; SFCC strings via JSON)

content.text:
# Mega Menu / Navigation: Contentful Schema + Docs + BM Investigation

Scope covered: Contentful content-type schema, `.docs/integration/`, docs-wide grep, `regional.md`, memory files, and Tier cross-check. I did **not** touch frontend component/hook code — that's the parallel agent's lane. All files below were read in full.

---

## 1. Contentful content-types inventory (`scripts/contentful/content-types/`)

All 8 files exist, all read in full:

| File | Relevant to nav? |
|---|---|
| `headerNavItem.js` | **Yes — core** |
| `headerNavigation.js` | **Yes — core** |
| `navGroup.js` | **Yes — core** |
| `link.js` | **Yes — core** |
| `image.js` | **Yes — plugs in via `promoImage`** |
| `region.js` | **Yes — regional scoping mechanism** |
| `footerConfig.js` | Adjacent (shares `navGroup`/`link`/`region`, not nav itself) |
| `uiCopy.js` | Not nav-related (generic string k/v store) |

**No `category`, `promo`, or `banner`-named content type exists.** Confirmed via `grep -n -i -E "categor|sfcc|commerce|business manager|\bBM\b" scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js` — zero matches for any SFCC/BM/category concept anywhere in the schema. The only cross-reference to SFCC at all is `region.js`'s `siteId` field, which is a join key for **site/region scoping**, not category data.

### Field summaries

**`headerNavItem.js`** (lines 1–76) — "A single top-level entry in the global header navigation — either a direct link (`href` set, no columns) or a mega-menu trigger (one or more columns of `navGroup` references, no `href`)." Fields: `label` (Symbol, required, localized), `href` (Symbol, optional — direct-link items only), `columns` (Array of `navGroup` entries — "0 columns = direct link via `href`... 1+ = mega-menu"), `twoColumnLayout` (Boolean, desktop/tablet-only side-by-side layout flag), `promoImage` (Link → `image` content type, optional), `regions` (Array of `region` entries, optional — "omitted/empty = applies to all regions"). Comment at line 26: "exactly one of `href` or a non-empty `columns` should be set on any given item, never both, never neither" — **documented as CMA-unenforceable**, not schema-validated.

**`headerNavigation.js`** (lines 1–33) — Root entry. "One default (unscoped) entry per locale, optionally overridden by additional entries scoped via `regions`." Fields: `internalTitle`, `items` (Array of `headerNavItem`, required), `regions` (Array of `region`, optional). Comment: "see `overrides/app/utils/resolveByRegion.ts`" for precedence — this is a frontend-code pointer I have not verified (parallel agent's territory).

**`navGroup.js`** (lines 1–37) — "A reusable 'heading + list of links' column — generalised from `footerNavGroup` so both the footer and the header mega-menu can reference the same shape." Fields: `internalTitle`, `heading` (optional, localized — "omitted means an unheaded group"), `showContactChannels` (Boolean, footer-only, "harmlessly unused by header mega-menu groups"), `links` (Array of `link`, required).

**`link.js`** (lines 1–25) — "A single reusable navigation link (label + destination)." Fields: `label` (Symbol, required, localized), `href` (Symbol, required, **free-text, not localized** — this is a plain string field, not a reference/link to any commerce entity), `regions` (optional scoping). Description explicitly states it's "designed to be referenced from other content types later (e.g. header nav, mega-menu) without change" — and per `navGroup.links`, it now is.

**`image.js`** (lines 1–65) — Reusable image primitive: `internalTitle`, `asset` (Asset link), `decorative` (Boolean, a11y), `altText`, `caption`, `link` (RichText, restricted to asset/entry/URL hyperlink nodes only, no marks). This is what `headerNavItem.promoImage` points to.

**`region.js`** (lines 1–41) — "One entry per SFCC storefront/region — the canonical, referenceable region entity." Fields: `siteId` (Symbol, required, unique — "matches an SFCC site ID from `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.generated.ts`'s `SITE_LOCALES` keys"), `label`, `locale` (informational only).

**`footerConfig.js`** / **`uiCopy.js`** — read in full for completeness; not nav-specific. `footerConfig.navGroups` references `navGroup` (confirms the shared-type unification, see finding below).

### Finding: a stale comment in the source-of-truth schema itself

`scripts/contentful/content-types/headerNavItem.js` lines 29–31 (in the `columns` field's comment block):

> "`navGroup` is authored on a separate branch (feature/contentful-navgroup-migration) and has no local file in this content-types/ directory yet — referenced here by content-type-ID string only, the same way footerConfig.js references 'footerNavGroup'."

This is **false as of the current repo state**, on two independent counts:
1. `navGroup.js` **does** exist in this same directory (I read it in full — see above).
2. `footerConfig.js` line 20 references `linkContentType: ['navGroup']`, **not** `'footerNavGroup'`.

`navGroup.js`'s own description (line 7) confirms it was "generalised from `footerNavGroup`," and `.docs/temp/SFCC-52-global-header-plan.md` line 870 confirms the old type was fully retired: *"Old `footerNavGroup` type + its 3 entries hard-deleted (with Tim's go-ahead)."* Git history corroborates the sequencing: `d934ad96 feat(contentful): unify footerNavGroup into shared navGroup type` predates `74653f50 feat(header): add headerNavItem/headerNavigation content types and useHeaderNav hook` in the merged history. **Net effect: this comment was accurate when written (on a not-yet-merged branch) but was never revisited after the merge, and now misdescribes the current schema to anyone reading it as documentation.** Not a functional bug (the schema itself works), but it's exactly the kind of "documented vs. actual" gap you asked me to flag.

---

## 2. `.docs/integration/` — Contentful and SFCC docs

**`.docs/integration/02-contentful.md`** — the one doc that directly addresses the question. Line 33, from the content-ownership table (§1):

> `| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | *Pending* |`

Columns are `Surface | SFCC owns | Contentful owns | Status`. This is the **only** place in `.docs/integration/` that states an ownership split for the mega menu — and it's explicitly marked **Pending**, i.e., not confirmed.

§10 "Open items requiring client confirmation," item 2 (lines 133–136):

> "**SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** ... Not yet confirmed is the split on composed pages: ... whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or built in Contentful Studio Experiences, and **whether the mega-menu includes Contentful-authored promotional tiles**. The working assumption is in the ownership table in §1."

`git log -- .docs/integration/02-contentful.md` shows 5 commits, none touching this table or open item — the text has not been revisited since it was first written, despite substantial nav/mega-menu implementation work happening later (see §3 below).

**`.docs/integration/01-sfcc.md`** — mentions categories only once, line 10, as one of several in-scope SCAPI resources: *"Product catalogue, categories, search, recommendations."* No further elaboration on category-tree structure or how it feeds navigation. Critically, line 24 lists as **explicitly out of scope of this document**: *"Business Manager configuration: promotions rules, content slots, Page Designer pages."* **01-sfcc.md deliberately does not document BM category-tree/navigation configuration at all** — this isn't an oversight, it's a stated scope boundary.

**Conclusion for step 2: no doc under `.docs/integration/` describes a mechanism for combining a BM category tree with Contentful content into the rendered mega menu.** The only doc that even frames the question (02-contentful.md) marks it explicitly unresolved.

---

## 3. Docs-wide grep — additional files found

Grepped `.docs/` for `menu|navigation|mega|category tree|flyout` (case-insensitive). Most hits were false positives (Measmerize/Didomi "SPA navigation," "Find in Boutique flyout" = a MuleSoft stock panel unrelated to the mega menu, generic "breadcrumb navigation," account left-nav, etc.) — I checked context on every hit before deciding relevance. Two genuinely new files surfaced beyond steps 1–2:

### `.docs/prd/homepage.md` — the authoritative confirmed PRD for nav UX (not the content-model mechanics)

§2 "Navigation" (HPC-022–HPC-025, HPC-029), lines 33–39:
- "Top-level categories link to PLP (HPC-022, confirmed — design dependency: each top-level item is either a mega menu trigger or a direct page link)"
- "**'Back in Boutique'** is a manually curated navigation category routing to its own PLP (HPC-023, confirmed)"
- "**Desktop**: mega menu on click, not hover (HPC-024, updated 2026-09-05 — design team instructed the change from hover to click; tracked via SFCC-883) — with the exception of **Z.Immerse**, which functions as a direct link to a page, not a mega menu trigger"
- "**Mobile**: hamburger menu (HPC-025, confirmed)"
- "The system supports **cloning of the global navigation structure across markets** (HPC-029, confirmed)"

Line 25 (Business users, §1): "Business users can add/remove navigation items without a code change (HPC-028, confirmed)."

This PRD documents **UX/interaction behaviour** (click-not-hover, mobile hamburger, CMS-manageability in principle) but says nothing about *whose data* (BM vs. Contentful) constitutes a nav item or its sub-links — that question is left entirely to 02-contentful.md, which (per §2 above) marks it Pending.

### `.docs/temp/SFCC-52-global-header-plan.md` — a 1445-line dev session log, not a confirmed doc, but it directly answers the "how do these combine" question

This is a working/scratch file (`.docs/temp/`), not one of the confirmed `.docs/prd/` or `.docs/integration/` docs — but since you asked me to flag whatever bears on this question, its "## Context" section (lines 966–1057) contains the single most direct answer in the whole repo, and it **conflicts with 02-contentful.md**:

Line 976 (story-scope table):
> "**SFCC-746** | Headline `Navigation` component (top-level nav bar) — supersedes SFCC-52's nav portion. **States top-level items come from SFCC BM category taxonomy (SFCC-28); team direction is Contentful instead** (see decisions below)."

Lines 1041–1047 (the key decision, under "Decisions confirmed with the user during planning"):
> "**Full Contentful replacement confirmed to also cover subcategory links, not just top-level items and images** — **SFCC-96 describes a hybrid model** (subcategories from SFCC BM taxonomy, only images/campaign content from Contentful) **and explicitly flags this as an open question itself** ('how does this work if categories are driven from BM, different images per locale in contentful etc'). Re-confirmed with the user: **proceed with full Contentful replacement everywhere** (`navGroup`'s links reference the generic `link` type, not SFCC categories) — **do not build the hybrid model SFCC-96's text describes.**"

And line 1010–1011:
> "Scope for this pass is everything: header shell, mega menu, mobile drawer nav, and **Contentful-driven nav content, full replacement (not an overlay on top of SFCC categories)**."

**What this means concretely, cross-checked against the schema I read in §1:** the actual technical design that was built is that `link.href` is a free-text Symbol field — an editor manually types/pastes a destination URL — with **no structural reference to any SFCC category ID or BM taxonomy node anywhere in the content model.** This is consistent with what I found in the schema (no category field exists anywhere in `headerNavItem.js`/`navGroup.js`/`link.js`).

**The conflict, stated plainly:** Two Jira tickets (SFCC-746, citing SFCC-28; and SFCC-96) describe/assume a BM-category-driven or hybrid nav model. A planning decision recorded in this temp session log overrides that in favour of pure Contentful authoring. But **`.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` — the actual integration design doc — was never updated to reflect this decision**: it still frames "Category tree" as SFCC-owned and the whole ownership split as "*Pending*." `.docs/temp/openItems.md` (lines 51–53) repeats the same not-yet-resolved framing almost verbatim, including the identical "how does this work if categories are driven from BM" language — confirming both docs are in sync with each other but **out of sync with the later decision** recorded in the temp plan file. Since `.docs/temp/` is a scratch/working-notes folder (not `.docs/prd/` or `.docs/integration/`), **nothing in the confirmed documentation set currently reflects the "full Contentful replacement" decision** — someone reading only `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` or `.docs/temp/openItems.md` would still believe this is an open question with an SFCC-category-tree-based working assumption.

I also confirmed the migration decision immediately preceding this (line 1024–1027): *"Unify the footer's `footerNavGroup` and the header's mega-menu column type into one shared `navGroup` content type... Requires migrating footer's existing usage; low risk since Contentful is still a mock/demo space, not production."* This is the direct origin of the stale-comment finding in §1.

Two additional relevant data points from the same file:
- Line 979: SFCC-97 (mobile expanded nav) — "Status: still design-dependent per the ticket itself."
- Line 980: SFCC-93 (header scroll behaviour) — "not yet confirmed by Zimmermann, no AC written."

I did not read this 1445-line file exhaustively beyond the sections directly answering your question (component-level CSS/motion/bug-fix detail throughout the rest of it is squarely the parallel agent's territory, not mine) — I did grep the full file for `Business Manager|\bBM\b|category tree|categoryId` to make sure I wasn't missing a second BM-specific discussion; the only hits were the ones quoted above.

### `.docs/temp/openItems.md` (lines 51–53)

Consolidated/aggregated version of 02-contentful.md's open item, worded almost identically: *"...whether the mega-menu carries Contentful-authored promotional tiles alongside the SFCC category tree. Zimmermann and merchandising to confirm the per-surface split..."* — confirms this open item is tracked consistently across two docs, both stale relative to the temp plan's decision.

### `.docs/prd/plp.md` line 153–156

"7. 'Back in Boutique' Navigation Category (HPC-022)" — *"A dedicated 'Back in Boutique' category in the navigation routes to its own PLP. Treat as a standard PLP filtered to this category — no other special behaviour confirmed."* Corroborates homepage.md's HPC-023 but adds nothing new on the BM/Contentful mechanism.

Everything else the grep surfaced (`.docs/integration/03-mulesoft.md`, `12-didomi.md`, `17-measmerize.md`, `.docs/vendor/measmerize.md`, `.docs/prd/search.md`, `giftcards.md`, `account.md`, `pdp.md`, `cart.md`) was generic UI-navigation or unrelated "flyout" panel language (Find in Boutique, SPA route changes) — checked and confirmed irrelevant to the mega-menu content model.

---

## 4. `.docs/prd/regional.md` — per-storefront nav differences

**Regional.md does not discuss per-storefront navigation/menu content differences at all.** I read the full file. It covers storefronts/URL prefixes, entry routing, checkout ownership, currency/tax, language, consent defaults, marketing opt-in, and GDPR — nothing about navigation structure varying (or not) by site. The closest related material lives elsewhere:
- `homepage.md` HPC-029 (already quoted in §3): "The system supports cloning of the global navigation structure across markets" — this is the only PRD statement on cross-market nav behaviour, and it's a **cloning** model (each market gets its own copy), not a shared-with-overrides model per se.
- The schema mechanism for this (§1): `headerNavigation.regions` / `headerNavItem.regions` / `link.regions`, each pointing to the `region` content type, with the documented precedence rule "omitted/empty = the default/global... A narrower-scoped entry takes precedence" (`headerNavigation.js` lines 26–29).
- `region.js`'s own doc comment confirms `siteId` "matches an SFCC site ID from `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.generated.ts`'s `SITE_LOCALES` keys" — i.e., region-scoping is keyed off SFCC site IDs, but this is a **site-scoping join key**, not a category-tree integration.

This is a genuine gap worth naming plainly: **no document explains how the mega menu's content differs (or is kept in sync) across the 8 storefronts beyond "it can be scoped per region and there's a cloning capability."** Whether Clothing/Accessories/Collections navGroups are independently authored per site or literally cloned/duplicated is not specified anywhere I found.

---

## 5. Memory files — done/in-progress/future-sprint status

**`.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`** (full file read): "Homepage & Navigation" appears under **Sprint 1** (line 28, "Part 1," 29 Jun–10 Jul) and **Sprint 2** (line 41, "Part 2," 13 Jul–24 Jul), both Squad A. Line 9: *"Contentful works/integration will be done as part of each corresponding functional story"* — no nav-specific detail. The file's own header (line 3) flags itself as *"Draft (2026-06-23). To be refined as sprints are confirmed."* Per my own prior memory (`project_real_sprint_cadence.md`), this sprint-dates draft is already known-stale against Jira ground truth (Sprint 3 = 11–24 Aug, not this doc's dates) — and the actual SFCC-52/746/96/97 dev work I found in §3 is dated late August (2026-08-25 through 08-31), well past this doc's Sprint 1/2 window. **sprintScope.md's placement of "Homepage & Navigation" in Sprint 1/2 is stale relative to when the work actually happened.**

**`.docs/memory/projectState.md`** (full file read, "Last updated: 2026-08-24"): **Does not mention SFCC-52, SFCC-746, SFCC-96, SFCC-97, or "mega menu" anywhere** — not in "What's Complete," "In Progress," or "What's Pending." The only header-related entry is generic: line 48, *"Header override... uppercase nav with `::after` hover animation... ## Bottom line — confirmed vs. silent

**Confirmed by the current Contentful schema (source of truth per this repo's own docs):** the mega menu's content model is `headerNavigation` → `headerNavItem[]` (each either a direct `href` or a `columns` array of `navGroup`) → `navGroup` (`heading` + `link[]`) → `link` (`label` + free-text `href`), with `region` entries providing per-storefront scoping and `image` providing the optional promo tile. **Nothing in this schema references an SFCC category ID, BM taxonomy node, or any commerce API.**

**Confirmed by a planning decision recorded in a non-authoritative temp session log** (`.docs/temp/SFCC-52-global-header-plan.md`, not a `.docs/prd/` or `.docs/integration/` doc): this absence is deliberate — the team explicitly rejected the BM-category/hybrid model that Jira tickets SFCC-746/SFCC-96/SFCC-28 describe, in favour of full Contentful ownership of the entire nav tree including subcategory links.

**Never updated to reflect that decision:** `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` (the actual integration design doc) and `.docs/temp/openItems.md` still both frame "SFCC owns the category tree, Contentful owns promo tiles only" as the **working assumption**, marked explicitly "**Pending**" client confirmation. `.docs/memory/projectState.md` (the project's official living-memory tracker) doesn't mention this work or decision at all, and is stale on mega-menu status generally.

**If you only read the confirmed docs** (`homepage.md`, `02-contentful.md`, `sprintScope.md`, `projectState.md`) **you would conclude this integration is still an open question with an SFCC-category-tree assumption on the table** — that gap between the confirmed docs and the as-built schema/decision is itself the key finding here, exactly as you anticipated.
